column1: discontinuance§Discontinuance of the line was announced in a footnote.§这条线路的**停运**是在一条脚注里宣布的。
discontinuity§There is a discontinuity in the rock face that dates the fault.§岩壁上有一处**断裂**，可用来确定断层的年代。
discord§A note of discord in the second movement is deliberate.§第二乐章里的一个**不和**谐音是有意为之。
discourteous§Answering a letter six months late is discourteous, not busy.§六个月才回信是**失礼**，不是忙。
discredit§He set out to discredit the witness and confirmed her instead.§他本想**诋毁**证人的可信度，结果反而证实了她。
discreet§A discreet cough from the doorway ended the meeting.§门口一声**克制**的咳嗽结束了会议。
discrepancy§A one-day discrepancy in the log changed the whole account.§日志上一天的**出入**改变了整个说法。
discrete§The signal is discrete, not continuous, and must be sampled.§这个信号是**离散的**而非连续的，必须采样。
discretion§Discretion is the better part of a first draft.§**审慎**是初稿最重要的品质。
discretionary§Discretionary spending was frozen and never unfrozen.§**可自由支配**的开支被冻结，再也没有解冻。
discriminating§Discriminating between the two hands takes a magnifier.§**区分**这两种笔迹需要放大镜。
disdain§He treats disdain as a form of argument.§他把**轻蔑**当作一种论证方式。
disenchant§Nothing disenchants faster than seeing how it is made.§没有什么比看到制作过程更快让人**幻灭**。
disgruntle§A disgruntled former employee kept the only complete copy.§一位**心怀不满**的前员工手里有唯一一份完整副本。
disguise§The building is a warehouse in the disguise of a chapel.§这座建筑是**伪装成**礼拜堂的仓库。
dishearten§Do not be disheartened by a first reader who missed the point.§不要因为第一位读者没读懂就**灰心**。
dishevel§She arrived disheveled, twenty minutes early, and completely prepared.§她**衣冠不整**地提前二十分钟到了，准备得非常充分。
disillusion§Disillusion arrived slowly and was, on balance, useful.§**幻灭**来得很慢，总的说来是有益的。
disincline§The fee disinclined exactly the readers it needed.§这笔费用恰恰**劝退**了它最需要的那批读者。
disingenuous§Her surprise was disingenuous; she had drafted the memo.§她的**惊讶是装的**，那份备忘录就是她起草的。
disjoint§Two disjoint sets share no member at all.§两个**不相交**的集合没有任何公共元素。
dislodge§Nothing could dislodge the idea once it was in print.§这个说法一旦印出来，就再也无法**撼动**。
dismantle§They dismantled the argument one footnote at a time.§他们一条脚注一条脚注地**拆解**了这个论证。
dismay§To his dismay the file had been correctly labeled all along.§让他**沮丧**的是，那份文件一直都贴对了标签。
dismissal§Dismissal of the appeal took four lines.§**驳回**上诉只用了四行字。
dismissive§Being dismissive of a question is not the same as answering it.§**轻慢**地对待一个问题不等于回答了它。
disorient§Fog disorients a walker faster than darkness does.§大雾比黑暗更快让步行者**迷失方向**。
disparage§He disparages his own drafts to forestall other people.§他先**贬低**自己的草稿，好抢在别人前面。
disparager§The book's chief disparager reviewed it three times.§这本书最主要的**贬抑者**评论了它三次。
disparate§Two disparate accounts turned out to describe the same afternoon.§两份**迥异**的叙述最后发现描述的是同一个下午。
disparity§The disparity is largest where the records are thinnest.§记录最稀薄的地方，**差距**也最大。
dispassionate§Be dispassionate about your own work only after it is finished.§只有在作品完成之后，才对它保持**冷静**。
dispatch§He dealt with the objection with remarkable dispatch.§他极其**迅速**地处理了那个反对意见。
dispel§One measurement dispelled a theory held for a century.§一次测量**驱散**了一个持续百年的理论。
dispersal§Dispersal of the crowd took longer than the speech.§**疏散**人群花的时间比演讲还长。
disperse§The ink disperses through the water in about a minute.§墨水大约一分钟就在水中扩**散开**。
dispersive§A dispersive medium spreads a pulse as it travels.§**色散**介质会使脉冲在传播中展宽。
displace§The new term displaced an older one within five years.§这个新术语五年内就**取代**了一个旧术语。
display§He made a display of reluctance and signed anyway.§他**做出一副不情愿的样子**，最后还是签了。
disposable§Disposable income, not price, decides what sells here.§决定这里什么好卖的是**可支配**收入，而非价格。
disposition§The disposition of the furniture had not changed since 1940.§家具的**摆放**自一九四〇年以来就没变过。
disputation§Medieval disputation was a public sport as much as a method.§中世纪的**辩论**既是一种方法，也是一项公开的竞技。
disputatious§A disputatious footnote can be more fun than the text.§一条**好争论的**脚注可能比正文更有趣。
disregard§He disregarded the warning and reached the summit anyway.§他**不顾**警告，最终还是登了顶。
disrepute§The word fell into disrepute and then came back.§这个词曾**名声不佳**，后来又回来了。
disrupt§Rain disrupted play for two hours on the second day.§第二天下雨**中断**了比赛两小时。
dissembler§Even a skilled dissembler leaves a paper trail.§即便是老练的**伪装者**也会留下纸面痕迹。
disseminate§Ideas disseminate faster than the corrections to them.§观念**传播**得比对它们的更正更快。
dissemination§Dissemination without attribution is how errors become facts.§不注明出处的**传播**，正是错误变成事实的方式。
dissension§Dissension in the ranks is easier to hide than to fix.§队伍里的**分歧**藏起来比解决它更容易。
dissipate§He dissipated a small fortune in under three years.§他不到三年就**挥霍**掉一小笔财产。
dissolute§The word dissolute says more about the writer than the subject.§“**放荡**”这个词说明作者的成分多过说明对象。
dissolve§Parliament was dissolved and an election called for June.§议会被**解散**，选举定在六月。
distaste§There is a distaste for detail that passes for high-mindedness.§有一种对细节的**嫌恶**，被当成了高远。
distillation§Distillation separates the two liquids by boiling point.§**蒸馏**依据沸点把两种液体分开。
distinct§I have the distinct impression we have met before.§我有一种**明确**的印象，我们以前见过。
distort§Fear distorts distance more reliably than fog.§恐惧比雾更能**扭曲**对距离的判断。
distortion§Distortion at the edges is a property of the lens, not the scene.§边缘的**畸变**是镜头的特性，不是景物的。
distract§A single loose thread distracted her for the whole performance.§一根松脱的线头让她整场演出都**分神**。
distraction§He took the job as a distraction and stayed nine years.§他把这份工作当作**消遣**，结果待了九年。
distribution§Distribution of the pamphlet was banned in two cities.§这本小册子在两个城市被禁止**分发**。
diversify§Diversify your sources before you trust the pattern.§在相信某种规律之前，先让你的资料来源**多样化**。
diversion§The diversion of funds was noticed only at the audit.§资金的**挪用**直到审计时才被发现。
diversity§Diversity of method matters as much as diversity of subject.§方法的**多样性**与题材的多样性同样重要。
divert§A good anecdote diverts an audience that has stopped listening.§一则好轶事能**吸引住**已经不再听的听众。
divisive§Divisive questions are often the only ones worth asking.§引起**分裂**的问题，往往才是唯一值得问的。
